> It does this:
> 
>   1. Detects OS/CPU: Linux/macOS/Windows, x64/arm64/arm.
>   2. Checks CPU/libc details:
>       - x64 AVX2 support
>       - Linux musl vs glibc
>   3. Chooses the right platform-specific optional package, e.g. opencode-linux-x64.
>   4. Copies or hard-links that package’s native binary into:
>      /root/.nvm/versions/node/v24.4.1/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/opencode.exe
>   5. Runs opencode.exe --version to verify it works.
>   6. If the right optional dependency is missing, it tries npm install --ignore-scripts --no-save in a temp directory to fetch it, copies the binary, then deletes the temp directory.
> 
>   On this machine, it installed opencode-ai@1.15.11, selected opencode-linux-x64, and bin/opencode.exe is a native Linux ELF binary reporting version 1.15.11.
> 
>   Security-wise: it does execute local system probes like ldd, and may run npm install as a fallback, which can access the npm registry. It does not appear to run arbitrary downloaded install scripts because it uses --ignore-scripts.

I spent some time trying to summarize all these and hopefully we all could find our conversation valuable for future decision:

### 1. What does modern LLM models support

| Provider | Latest Model | Context Window | Max Output Tokens 
|----------|--------------|-----------------|-------------------|
| **OpenAI** | GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.4 | ~1,000,000 tokens | **128,000** | 
| **Anthropic** | Claude Opus 4.7 | 1,000,000 tokens | **128,000** (sync) / **300,000** (Batch API) | 
| **Google** | Gemini 3.5 Flash | ~1,000,000 tokens | **65,536** | 
| **DeepSeek** | DeepSeek V4 Pro | 1,000,000 tokens | **384,000** | 

### 2. Claude Code and Codex CLI current mechanism

**Claude Code** lets the model cap drive output (from online tech doc):
- `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`  'Set the maximum number of output tokens for most requests. Defaults and caps vary by model;' env var defaults to model's own max output (128k Opus 4.7, 64k Sonnet 4.6)
- Sync API: up to model max,  Batch API: up to 300k via `output-300k-2026-03-24` beta header
- Docs: [code.claude.com/env-vars](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) → [platform.claude.com/models](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview)

**OpenAI Codex CLI** hardcodes 128k for all GPT-5 models (from github info):
- `max_output_tokens: 128_000` in `codex-rs/core/src/openai_model_info.rs`
- Users hit `stream disconnected before completion: reason: max_output_tokens` (GitHub issue [#14753](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/14753))
- Not user-configurable — feature requested in issue [#20861](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/20861)
- Source: [codex-rs/openai_model_info.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/openai_model_info.rs) (mentioned by issue [#3523](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/3523))

### 3. Possible directions

**Option 1** Maintain current behavior and allow global config to adjust max output tokens.

**Option 2** Allow per-model max output tokens overrides.

**Option 3** Allow per-profile or per-job configuration. As someone may want aggressively truncated tool call output for certain projects. Others might need larger windows for long run tasks like log analysis and self driven code generation, etc.

Still reproducing on **opencode 1.15.11** with a different plugin (`opencode-goal-plugin@0.1.8`), so dropping a fresh repro here in case it helps maintainers prioritize the coalescer fix.

### Repro

1. opencode 1.15.11, plugin `opencode-goal-plugin@0.1.8`.
2. Provider: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` -> self-hosted vLLM serving Qwen3.5-122B-A10B with the upstream chat template.
3. Run `/goal <anything>` in a session.
4. Request fails immediately with `AI_APICallError` and response body `"System message must be at the beginning."`.

### Wire payload (from opencode's own debug log)

```json
"messages": [
  { "role": "system", "content": "You are opencode, an interactive CLI tool ..." },
  { "role": "system", "content": "<goal_continuation>\n...\n<goal_objective>\ndraw a ball\n</goal_objective>\n..." },
  { "role": "user",   "content": "draw a ball" }
]
```

Two `role: "system"` messages. The Qwen3.5 chat template raises on the second one (`raise_exception('System message must be at the beginning.')`), vLLM returns 400, opencode surfaces it as `AI_APICallError`.

### Why this is opencode's bug (not just the plugin's)

The compiled binary shows opencode *intends* to coalesce plugin-added system blocks after `experimental.chat.system.transform` fires, but the guard is off-by-one — coalescing only runs when `system.length > 2`, so the common case of *one* plugin pushing *one* block (final length = 2) goes straight through to the provider as two separate `role: "system"` messages.

Decompiled snippet from the 1.15.11 binary:

```js
const o = r[0];
yield* A.plugin.trigger("experimental.chat.system.transform", ..., { system: r });
if (r.length > 2 && r[0] === o) {        // ← should be `> 1`
    const C = r.slice(1);
    r.length = 0;
    r.push(o, C.join("\n"));
}
```

Until this is fixed upstream, any plugin doing `output.system.push(...)` (the documented hook usage pattern) silently breaks strict-template backends.

### Candidate fix already exists

cyrilmhansen/opencode#2 was merged to that fork on 2026-03-26 with exactly the right shape — collapse `system` fragments into a single newline-joined system message before provider request construction. It does **not** appear to have landed on `anomalyco/opencode` `dev` yet, and 1.15.11 still ships the broken coalescer. Any blockers to rebasing and merging it?

### Plugin-side report filed in parallel

I've also filed willytop8/OpenCode-goal-plugin#1 asking the plugin to merge into `system[0]` defensively instead of `push`-ing, per the guidance requested in #23660. That fix is independent and gives users on strict backends a path forward without waiting on the upstream coalescer.

### Environment

- opencode: 1.15.11
- Plugin: opencode-goal-plugin@0.1.8
- Provider: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`
- Backend: vLLM 0.19.x, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B Hybrid INT4/FP8
- OS: Linux 6.17 aarch64 (NVIDIA GB10)

Quick A/B validation of the plugin-side workaround against my reproducer (opencode 1.15.11 + goal-plugin 0.1.8 + Qwen3.5-122B vLLM):

| Plugin code | Result |
|---|---|
| `output.system.push(...)` (current goal-plugin behavior) | HTTP 400 `"System message must be at the beginning."` |
| Merge into `output.system[0]` (patched locally in the plugin file) | Request succeeded, model executed tools, session continued normally |

This confirms both:

1. The user-visible bug is **avoidable by plugins today** if they follow the documented merge pattern (per #23660).
2. But it **shouldn't have to be** — every plugin author would have to learn this gotcha. The right durable fix is still the coalescer change in opencode core (cyrilmhansen/opencode#2 shape), so plugins can keep using the natural `output.system.push` pattern that the hook signature suggests.

Tracking the plugin-side fix at willytop8/OpenCode-goal-plugin#1 to unblock users now while the upstream coalescer fix lands.
